scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem; an AI agent that auto-answers disputes and auto-fixes billing will resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused valid meter reads to be rejected or misclassified, forcing estimate substitution and producing wrong bills that drive disputes.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The vendor-run AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) began delivering missing or invalid interval reads since August, causing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reading (H-FIELD-BILL, contracted to MeterWorks) degraded in completeness or timeliness since August, causing missing reads, estimate substitution, and billing errors.

H-USAGE-DRIVEN-DISPUTES.statement: Bills issued since August are largely correct, but a usage or tariff change increased amounts owed, prompting more disputes without any underlying meter-to-cash error.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: The majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry ACTUAL read type, suggesting a large share of disputes stem from billing calculation, tariff, or amount issues on correctly-read accounts rather than estimate substitution from read failures.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reader staffing shortfall (three readers short) since July is the specific driver behind late manual-read routes, causing estimate substitution and billing errors for affected customers.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data shows median ticket response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, indicating ticket response handling is not slow relative to the stated SLA. This weighs against the premise that the dispute surge is caused by slow/inadequate response handling.

Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, a shortfall touching 9200 manual-read accounts. This indicates manual meter reads were materially incomplete during the dispute-surge window, consistent with missed reads feeding estimate substitution and wrong bills.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (3025 total), so 59% of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL (non-substituted) read, not an estimated one. This means estimate-substitution causal chains (AMI export failure, field read failure, rule-change rejection) can at most account for the minority of disputed bills; the majority of disputes occur on bills where a real meter read was used.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes are recorded in the system during the period covered by the log. This removes a tariff-rate-change explanation for the dispute surge, leaving only a possible usage-volume (non-tariff) component of H-USAGE-DRIVEN-DISPUTES unaddressed.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, a non-authoritative stakeholder, claims there has been no tariff change this year, which agrees with the already-recorded authoritative finding E-04 (zero tariff changes in billing-db's log) and does not add new decision-relevant information.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and the affected customers' bills to be estimated instead of actually read. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for the already-observed route completion shortfall (E-02) and the estimate-substitution pathway, but it is a non-authoritative stakeholder statement from someone with a stated incentive to secure a contract headcount increase, so it is uncorroborated by any system-of-record data.

CRM monthly dispute counts (610 in 2026-06, 590 in 2026-07, 1180 in 2026-08, 1260 in 2026-09) confirm with authoritative tool data that ticket volume roughly doubled starting in August, matching the magnitude/timing of the initial complaint but saying nothing about cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution occurs only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this reinforces the existing human-approval requirement for push_route_update rather than granting anyone authority to execute route changes automatically.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query shows 320 distinct accounts received an ESTIMATED read in the most recent billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000 on R-00). This gives account-to-route linkage for currently-estimated accounts but, by itself, does not indicate whether estimation is concentrated on specific routes (consistent with a localized staffing shortage) or spread broadly, and says nothing about cause.

U-CALC-DEFECT-TYPE.question: What specific billing-calculation/amount defect (rate application, consumption calc, proration, fee) causes disputes on ACTUAL-read accounts?
U-CALC-DEFECT-TYPE.decision_impact: Determines which billing rule or calculation path must be fixed; no bill correction can be scoped or authorized without it.
U-CALC-DEFECT-TYPE.resolution_path: Run diagnose_billing_calculation_defect against DA-BILL line items and review_billing_rule_change_log against DA-RULES to isolate the mechanism.
U-CALC-DEFECT-TYPE.safe_placeholder: Ship only diagnostic investigation; perform no bill write until the defect mechanism is documented and reviewed by Billing Operations.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.question: Is the field route completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-02) actually caused by the staffing shortage SH-FIELD claims, or another factor, and does it materially explain the minority ESTIMATED-read disputes?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any route update is warranted and what to request; SH-FIELD's claim is uncorroborated and carries a stated headcount incentive.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-check route-log completion records against scheduling/staffing data independent of SH-FIELD's statement before proposing any route update.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Investigate only; propose no route_update until the shortfall cause is corroborated beyond the stakeholder claim.

U-AMI-EXPORT-COVERAGE.question: With vendor AMI/MDMS export access pending (mdms-export DEGRADED), could undetected AMI read issues still contribute to part of the ESTIMATED-read disputes not addressed by E-03?
U-AMI-EXPORT-COVERAGE.decision_impact: If AMI issues exist, the estimate-substitution minority pathway may need a vendor-side fix in addition to the field-staffing hypothesis.
U-AMI-EXPORT-COVERAGE.resolution_path: Pursue vendor-provisioned mdms-export access and re-run read-type/coverage analysis once available.
U-AMI-EXPORT-COVERAGE.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI contribution as unconfirmed; do not rely on or rule out AMI-side causes until export access is restored.

U-SUCCESS-BASELINE-DEFINITION.resolution_path: Confirm with SH-CS/SH-BILL whether the Jun-Jul average (E-07) or a defined accuracy-audit threshold is the operative baseline.
U-SUCCESS-BASELINE-DEFINITION.safe_placeholder: Use the Jun-Jul 2026 monthly average (~600, E-07) as a provisional baseline target until an explicit baseline is confirmed.
